This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices. It fetches the source from the declared upstream repository (https://github.com/insim-ai/InSpice) at a specific tagged version (`v$pkgver`), builds a Python wheel using `python -m build`, and installs it via `python -m installer` into `$pkgdir`. The `prepare()` function runs `git clean -dfx` within the source directory, which is a routine practice to ensure a clean build environment. No suspicious commands (eval, base64, curl, wget, etc.), no obfuscated code, no network requests to unexpected hosts, no file operations outside the standard build/install scope, and no data exfiltration are present. One minor note: the `sha256sums` entry contains an explicit hash rather than `'SKIP'` for a git-based source, which is unconventional (git sources typically use SKIP since tag refs can be mutated). However, this is a packaging hygiene concern, not evidence of malicious behavior, and the hash itself does not introduce any threat.
